To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have isolated a human cerebellar specific TASK gene, TASK-3, that is inhibited by acidosis.
a novel human two pore domain potassium gene, TASK-3, has been isolated and localised to 8q24, and shown to be cerebellar specific.
(i) We have cloned and characterised a human TASK-3 gene which encodes a novel two pore-domain potassium channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular cloning, functional expression and localisation of a novel human two-pore domain K(+) channel, TASK-3.
the identification of a new human two pore domain potassium gene, which has a specific tissue expression pattern and a unique functional profile.
a novel member of the human two pore domain family of potassium channels which is cerebellum specific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human TASK-1 and TASK-3 are two separate genes which encode two separate proteins, with distinct and different functions, and with distinct and different tissue expression patterns.
the human TASK-3 gene has been cloned and its expression localised to the cerebellum.
we have cloned and characterised the first human TASK-3 gene, and have demonstrated that this is expressed in a very cerebellum-specific manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned, localised and functionally expressed a new member of the human TASK gene family, human TASK-3.
we have identified a human gene which has the potential to be an excellent target for drug development.
human TASK-2, TASK-3 and TASK-5 genes are expressed in the cerebellar cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human TASK-1 and TASK-3 are not orthologous, as was previously thought, but that human TASK-2 is the ortholog of rat TASK-2.
the human TASK-3 gene is cerebellum-specific and is a novel member of the TASK gene family.
we have cloned and characterised the third TASK channel from humans.
